title: Fix delayed prefetch attribution and revert negative invoice adjustments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported unexpected negative invoice adjustments and month-to-date credit spikes after rolling back a streaming prefetch optimization. The behavior occurs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Root cause appears to be delayed attribution of prefetched token emissions combined with out-of-order ledger writes during regional failover and KV rehydrate. Users saw reversed charges (credits) applied days after initial consumption, leading to billing deltas and urgent escalations.

Background: We implemented a prefetch optimization that emits token accounting for anticipated prefixes to warm KV caches and reduce tail-latency. On normal flow, prefetched tokens are tagged with a short-lived sentinel and reconciled when the real request hits. During a regional failover and a scheduled KMS rotation in some Private clusters, the reconciliation pipeline wrote the sentinel-prefetch ledger rows after the canonical request rows, which caused the downstream billing exporter to treat them as late negatives and apply credits. Additionally, Dedicated warmup appliances that replayed cache snapshots on restart emitted dedup keys without the tenant namespace when disk snapshots were recovered, creating cross-tenant attribution edge cases.

Impact: Affected customers saw negative invoice adjustments ranging from a few dollars to multiple kUSD on high-volume tenants. Several customers opened P1/P0 escalations with support and finance. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigation, and production-safe rollout of the fix and compensating reconciliation for any misapplied credits.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Asha Patel (creator): Initial customer report from AcmeAnalytics: automated refund/credit of $9.2k appeared in month-to-date reconciliation. Support created CR-845 and escalated to engineering. Observed credits tied to 'prefetch' reason code in ledger exports.

2026-03-02 — Liam Ortega (assignee): Reproduced locally by replaying ingestion stream under an artificially delayed CDC ordering. Confirmed that prefetch sentinel rows are sometimes emitted with timestamps > canonical request when failover triggers cache rehydrate. Attached reproduction harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pull/62

2026-03-03 — Marco Chen (runtime): Discovered Dedicated warmup service (warmupd) was restoring KV snapshots and emitting 'warmup_count' events with an empty tenant_id when snapshot metadata was corrupted during an upgrade. This caused the ledger apportioner to route credits to fallback tenant-bucket and later reconcile them as negative adjustments. Creating ENG-158433 to harden warmupd snapshot validation.

2026-03-04 — Evelyn Smith (billing): Short-term mitigation: disabled prefetch emitter for Hosted and Dedicated in region-eu-west-2 and queued a one-off re-export of ledger rows from the canonical store for March 1-3. Finance paused automated credit application pending reconciliation. Linked internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Prefetch+Credit+Runbook

2026-03-05 — Liam Ortega: Root cause summary draft: (1) prefetch emitter does not persist canonical-request link id reliably when rehydrate fails; (2) CDC pipeline allowed out-of-order commit of prefetch rows during replay; (3) billing exporter treats late prefetch rows with negative delta semantics. Proposed changes: persist strong parent_request_id on prefetch rows, add sequence numbers, and modify exporter to ignore prefetch deltas older than X minutes unless reconciled. See design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/billing/reconcile-prefetch-2026-03-05

2026-03-06 — QA (Jin Park): Integration tests added to verify ledger ordering and exporter tolerance. Created test vectors: high-latency failover, KMS rotation with rehydrate, and dedicated warmup snapshot corruption. Test run: https://ci.redwood.ai/blue/organizations/jenkins/billing-reconcile-tests/detail/PR-197/1/pipeline

2026-03-08 — Liam Ortega: Implemented defensive checks and sequence-number enforcement in prefetch emitter (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4217). Also added exporter change to treat isolated prefetch rows as non-crediting unless reconciled within recon_window=72h. Rolling patch to staging for smoke tests.

2026-03-09 — Oncall (Nina Gomez): Staging smoke tests look good. Began canary rollout to 10% of Hosted traffic in us-east-1 and one Dedicated pool. Observed stable token_accounting delta rates and no new negative adjustments in the canary cohort. Monitoring dashboard: https://datadog.redwood.ai/dash/billing/prefetch-reconcile

2026-03-10 — Finance & Support coordination (Asha): Preparing customer-facing remediation plan. For customers with confirmed misapplied credits, finance will reverse the erroneous credits and apply corrected invoices, with clear communication and goodwill credit where appropriate. List of impacted customers exported to secure drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/financials/prefetch_incidents_2026-03-10.csv
reproduction_steps:
1) Enable prefetch emitter and start high-throughput streaming session against region A.
2) Trigger simulated failover to region B while performing KMS rotation on a Private cluster (use the repro harness to delay CDC ordering).
3) Observe ledger emission order: if prefetch sentinel rows are emitted after canonical request rows, billing exporter will apply late negative deltas.
4) Run billing exporter against the replayed ledger to validate negative credit behavior. The repro harness and scripts are in the linked PR.
root_cause: Race between prefetch emitter and CDC/rehydration paths: prefetch rows lacked an invariant parent_request_id and sequence ordering. During rehydrate/failover windows and snapshot restores (especially in Private deployments with KMS rotation), prefetch rows were committed after canonical request rows and treated by the exporter as late negative adjustments. Dedicated warmup snapshot corruption amplified cross-tenant attribution errors.
fix_plan:
Short-term: disable prefetch emitter for at-risk regions/pools and re-export canonical ledger rows for affected windows; hold automated credit application.
Medium-term: require parent_request_id and per-request sequence numbers on all prefetch emissions; make billing exporter idempotent to prefetch sentinel rows (ignore or queue as reconciled items).
Long-term: add CI for ledger ordering invariants, strengthen warmupd snapshot metadata validation, and add observability (reconcile lag SLO and alerting).
rollback_plan: If the new exporter change causes regressions, revert exporter to previous behavior and re-enable disabled emitters only after rollback. All reverts must be coordinated with Finance to avoid doubling corrections. Keep canary window and monitor negative_adjustment_rate metric before full rollout.
qa_tests:
- Integration test vectors simulating delayed CDC ordering and KMS rotation.
- End-to-end billing export simulation comparing canonical vs exported deltas.
- Canary monitoring for negative_adjustment_rate and tenant_credit_flap_count.
- Manual verification with two impacted customer accounts in staging.
